sentences.text: I. A. No.1393 of 2023 is an application seeking for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed by the sole appellant - Virendra Kumar Parihar, who has been convicted under Section 376AB of the Indian Penal Code and also convicted under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default R.I. for 2 years vide impugned judgment dated 28.10.2021 passed by the XXIII Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012), Bhopal in Special Case No.600 of 2021.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the prosecution is that on 18.02.2020 at about 7:30 P.M. the complainant namely the mother of the victim was along with the victim as well as PW-8, PW-10 and PW-14 on the second floor of the building where they reside.
After some time she received a phone call from her husband and in order to answer the same, she went inside her home.
After 15-20 minutes thereafter, when she returned to the place where the victim was playing, she did not find her there.
She went in search of her.

Thereafter the victim came down the stairs crying and told her that one "Bhaiya" had taken her to the terrace of the said building by inducing her to show a pigeon and inserted his finger in her anus and vagina and made her eat his stool.

On the basis of the said information, the case was registered in F.I.R. No.203 of 2020 for offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(3) of the I.P.C.
and Sections 5 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
On trial, the appellant was convicted and sentenced under the aforementioned offences.
Thereafter, the instant appeal was filed.
Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the prosecution has failed to make out the case against the appellant.

That even if the prosecution case is to be accepted, it cannot be said that he has committed an offence as defined under Section 376 of the I.P.C. That he has already undergone a sentence of more than 3 years 3 months.
Hence, he may be released on bail.
The same is disputed by the learned Public Prosecutor placing reliance on the evidence of the witnesses.
He submits that the prosecution has established its case beyond all reasonable doubt against the appellant.
That even the victim has identified the accused.

Hence, he is not entitled for suspension of sentence and grant Virendra Kumar Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53390401/
1 of bail.

sentences.text: On the previous date, notice was issued to the complainant.
The office note indicates that the notice has been served.
Even then none represents the complainant.
Heard learned counsels.
The material on record would indicate the manner in which the offence has been committed.
It is stated that the victim has also identified the accused.
His contention is that the DNA does not support the prosecution case and that even in the F.I.R. the appellant's name has not been shown but the name of one "Devendra Bhaiya" is shown.
This aspect of the matter has not been considered.
That the appellant has been wrongly convicted.
The same requires to be considered at the stage of final hearing of the matter.
For the present, it is suffice to notice that the identity of the appellant itself is under doubt.

Even though the trial court has come to the conclusion that the appellant has committed the offence, the very plea of the defence that the name as shown in the FIR and as identified by the victim is not the appellant but someone else, requires to be considered by this Court.
Furthermore, the appellant has already undergone the sentence of more than 3 years and 3 months.
Hence, we are of the view that it is a fit case where the sentence should be suspended and bail should be granted.
Consequently, the application (I.A. No.1393 of 2023) is allowed.

Appellant - Virendra Kumar Parihar is enlarged on bail subject to he depositing the fine amount and furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court/concerned Court on 21.08.2023 and thereafter on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.
In view of the Covid-19, the Jail Authorities are directed to follow the Covid-19 protocol as per the Government guidelines before releasing the appellant on bail.

(RAVI MALIMATH) (VISHAL M  CHIEF JUSTICE JUDG  psm Date: 2023.04.21 18:46:58 +05'30'
